prompt: Scenario 1: A system that automatically turns off the lights in an office building at 7 p.m. every weekday. Which solution is most appropriate?
explanation: A rule-based automation (simple cron script) is ideal because the condition is fixed, binary, and deterministic (time = 7 p.m. AND day = weekday). Introducing an LLM agent would add unnecessary cost, latency, and failure points without any benefit.

prompt: Scenario 2: A system that responds to customer email inquiries, categorizes them, and escalates complex cases to a human while adapting from past interactions. Which solution is most appropriate?

options.text: A rigid rule-based script with static keywords
An LLM-powered AI agent with tools and memory

explanation: This requires understanding unstructured natural language, contextual decision-making (assessing sentiment and urgency), and maintaining memory over multi-turn interactions—classic hallmarks for an LLM-powered agent.

prompt: Scenario 3: A financial compliance system that flags any single transaction exceeding $10,000 for manual review. Which solution is most appropriate?
explanation: This is a strictly defined, unambiguous threshold rule. A simple deterministic check (`if amount > 10000: flag()`) is fast, cheap, audit-proof, and 100% reliable.

prompt: Arrange the architectural eras of AI agent evolution in chronological order (earliest to latest):

items.text: Rule-Based Systems (Fixed logic, explicit expert rules like MYCIN)
Learning-Based Agents (Reinforcement learning, trial & error like AlphaGo)
LLM-Powered Agents (Zero-shot generalization, natural language reasoning & tool use)

explanation: Agent evolution progressed from 1970s hand-coded expert systems, to trial-and-reward RL optimization in the 2010s, to modern LLM-driven reasoning engines capable of open-domain tool usage.
